glosses: The act of tying or binding something.
A cord or similar thing used to tie something; especially the thread used in surgery to close a vessel or duct.

examples.text: He hid shoelaces or rope under cushions to use as ligatures.
anti-ligature clothing
examples.translation: (in psychiatry) clothing that prevents one from using it to tie knots
examples.english: (in psychiatry) clothing that prevents one from using it to tie knots

examples.text: I likewiſe felt ſeveral ſlender Ligatures acroſs my Body, from my Armpits to my Thighs. I could only look upwards, the Sun began to grow hot, and the Light offended mine Eyes.

glosses: A thread or wire used to remove tumours, etc.
The state of being bound or stiffened; stiffness.

examples.text: the ligature of a joint

glosses: A character that visually combines multiple letters, such as æ, œ, ß or ĳ; also logotype. Sometimes called a typographic ligature.
A group of notes played as a phrase, or the curved line that indicates such a phrase.
A curve or line connecting notes; a slur.
A piece used to hold a reed to the mouthpiece on woodwind instruments.
Any binding, uniting, or restraining principle or agency.
A spell or charm that induces sexual impotence.

examples.text: The Roman epic poet Vergil refers to the incapacitating effects of ligatures, while Ovid, the erotic poet, admits the power of such spell-bindings.

examples.text: Il résolut de se louer comme rameur pour gagner sa vie et entretenir sa mère. Il reçut d’avance 40 ligatures du patron du bateau et les emporta avec lui avec l’idée d’acheter quelques pacotilles qu’il revendrait avec bénéfice.
